method.inspection: Viewed both final infographic PNGs and every native PowerPoint slide PNG individually. Also viewed the Aha English 390px HTML screenshot as supplementary visual context.
method.reading_size_assessment: Infographics inspected at full available image detail. Intended-size assessments are reasoned from the supplied native dimensions and proportional text scaling, not newly generated scaled raster screenshots or human usability tests.
method.source_access: None. No source exploration, author scripts, export, installs, remote browsing, or source edits.
method.animation_limit: Stills establish consecutive causal build slides only. They do not establish native animated-object motion or interactive behavior.
method.editability_limit: Native textbox editing validation was reported by the parent; it was not repeated in this review.

summary.verdict: Focused corrections required before the Aha media is release-ready. ANC has a small infographic label-clearance issue but no blocking defect observed in its nine slide renders.
positive_observations: Both decks use dark opening/closing slides and substantially lighter, readable body slides.
The ANC sequence exposes the mechanism progressively rather than presenting only generic topic cards.
Aha includes concrete ANC and Git history examples, with numeric residuals and visible commit-state diagrams.
No slide-edge text clipping or body-text/shape collision was observed across the 19 individual slide renders.
Causal builds should be described as consecutive slides, not as native object animation.

findings.location: First numbered section, heading above the workflow blocks
findings.observation: The heading 'Bound research -> authored source' wraps to a second line and extends past its reserved heading region into/across the horizontal divider. The section boundary visibly interferes with the heading.
findings.impact: Broken hierarchy and a visible collision in a primary explanatory section, at both native and reduced reading size.
findings.recommendation: Reserve a genuine two-line heading area and move the divider and workflow down together, or shorten the heading to a single line. Recheck the next section boundary after redistribution; do not merely shrink the heading.

findings.location: Infographic footer and closing slide bottom-left footer
findings.observation: The infographic retains 'visual QA pending'. The closing slide footer reads 'Fresh Aha source edition · commit 31ff1331 · actual media QA still pending'.
findings.impact: Final audience-facing media exposes an internal unfinished-review status. The deck has the same problem beyond the infographic already noted by the parent.
findings.recommendation: Remove workflow status from audience-facing footers. Retain only useful provenance, if desired, and keep review state in the delivery/QA record. Do not replace it with an unsupported approval or human-testing claim.
findings.parent_reported_previously: Infographic only; closing-slide occurrence independently observed.

findings.location: Small captions, mechanism annotations, matrix text, and footer across the tall infographic
findings.observation: At a 540px display width, the hierarchy and main explanatory text remain plausible for scrollable reading, but the smallest labels are already comparatively fine. At 390px, the 1080px-wide artwork scales to about 36%: smaller native labels in the low/mid-20px range become approximately 8-10px, and much supporting text becomes roughly 11-12px.
findings.impact: At 390px, the overall structure remains recognizable but sustained reading of diagram labels and supporting explanations requires zoom. Scrolling alone does not solve the reduced type size.
findings.recommendation: Treat 540px as the provisional minimum no-zoom presentation width, subject to actual-device verification. For 390px delivery, use the responsive HTML explanation or a purpose-built narrow layout with larger text and stacked mechanism panels rather than downscaling this single PNG.
findings.confidence: high for scaling risk; no actual-device usability test performed
findings.condition: This is a defect only if the PNG is expected to be comfortably readable without zoom at 390px. It is not a mobile requirement imposed on the ANC infographic.

findings.location: Left side of the first mechanism row, 'Incoming noise' label and nearby waveform crest
findings.observation: The waveform crest reaches the bottom of the 'Incoming noise' label region, leaving effectively no visual separation around the end of the label.
findings.impact: A small but visible text/graphic crowding point; the label remains decipherable. Reduced desktop display makes the contact more apparent.
findings.recommendation: Move the label slightly upward or the waveform slightly downward to create a clear, consistent gap while preserving the arrow alignment into the microphone.

findings.observation: The multi-curve waveform uses differing colors/styles, but the compact panel does not identify the individual curves as explicitly as the slide example does. A reader of this standalone PNG must infer which trace is incoming noise, anti-noise, or the sum.
findings.impact: The example communicates that cancellation is involved, but decoding the actual mechanism depends on prior knowledge rather than an immediate label-to-curve mapping.
findings.recommendation: Add short direct labels or a compact legend for noise, anti-noise, and sum. Keep it within the panel and large enough for the intended 540px width; avoid adding a tiny footer legend.

observations: Mechanism flow, waveform comparison, mismatch example, practical boundaries, and source footer are visibly organized into distinct regions.
At the intended two-thirds scaling, body and source text remain reasoned desktop-readable; no mobile acceptance criterion was applied.
The narrow waveform/label clearance is the only concrete layout issue identified.
No clipped right-edge flow label, bottom footer collision, or obvious low-contrast body text was observed.
The vertical numbered sections make the workflow and examples easy to locate.
The heading/divider collision is visible at native resolution and is not simply a small-screen issue.
540px is materially more plausible for reading than 390px, particularly for compact captions and matrix entries.
The actual mechanism examples are useful; label clarity should be improved without replacing them with generic icons.

slide_reviews.observations: Dark opening bookend. Headline and supporting statement have sufficient contrast and separation; no visible clipping.
Light body layout. Explanatory blocks, labels, and connectors remain distinct; no unintended overlap or footer collision observed.
Initial causal build is readable. De-emphasized later-stage content is an intentional build cue, not a failed foreground-contrast state.
Next waveform build cleanly separates plot and explanation. Caption provides model context. No collision with graph or footer observed.
Cancellation outcome is visibly distinguished from the preceding build. Diagram and text regions remain readable with no clipping.
Mismatch/residual explanation has clear hierarchy and a readable numeric takeaway. Waveforms remain inside their plotting region.
Practical mechanism/control content remains legible. Labels do not collide with neighboring blocks or connector geometry.
Practical limitations are separated clearly. Body text and lower source line have adequate space; no uncontrolled wrapping observed.
Dark closing bookend is readable. Main takeaway and supporting lines fit; no analogous pending-QA footer leakage observed.
Dark opening slide has clear title hierarchy, high-contrast text, and no visible overflow.
Workflow boxes and arrows are separated cleanly. Wrapped labels remain contained; no overlap analogous to the infographic heading was observed.
Research/source explanation is readable. Source-document filenames functioning as citations are not, by themselves, unfinished-QA leakage.

Concrete ANC plot and numeric result are readable. Minor clarity opportunity: make normalized axis meaning explicit for readers unfamiliar with the model; this is not a release-blocking rendering failure.
The residual/mismatch comparison is visibly different from the preceding state and retains readable explanatory text and curve identification.

Git mechanism states and arrow routing remain comprehensible. The rightmost result box has a tighter outer margin than the left side but is not clipped; no fix is required solely for stylistic symmetry.
Following Git state/build remains distinguishable and readable. Stills illustrate the state change but cannot verify any button interaction mentioned by the example.
Review/medium guidance fits in its regions. The artifact-qa document reference reads as a source citation, not a pending-status assertion.
Longer supporting wording still fits without colliding with neighboring regions or the footer.

Dark closing slide has readable high-contrast rows. The title wraps to two lines but retains a clear gap above the RESEARCH row, so the wrap itself is not a bug. The bottom-left 'actual media QA still pending' text must be removed from final delivery.

supplementary_review.observations: Viewed the supplied narrow HTML screenshot. Its stacked responsive presentation provides useful context for preferring HTML rather than forcing the full-width infographic into 390px. No additional high-confidence collision was identified in this supplementary screenshot.
supplementary_review.not_assessed: No interaction, live browser state, or behavior was tested. Other optional HTML screenshots were not inspected and are not included in the all-slides coverage claim.

next_verification: After focused layout fixes, re-render and inspect the Aha infographic heading/divider and subsequent section positions.
Check the final Aha infographic and closing-slide footers for removal of pending-QA language.
Verify ANC infographic label/wave clearance at 1200x800.
If claiming 390px PNG readability, verify an actual resized or actual-device presentation after a dedicated narrow-layout change; this review does not support that claim.
This is a first-pass review record, not evidence that fixes have already been applied or passed.
